subject: Post-call: residency constraints & logs — Sunrise Health follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: residency constraints & logs — Sunrise Health follow-up

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and the things we promised to follow up on so your security/compliance team can evaluate fit: 

Summary from call
- Primary ask: ensure patient-identifiable data used for inference is stored and processed within US-only infrastructure, with EU/APAC used only in DR scenarios under explicit controls.
- Logging: you need request/response-level audit logs for 90 days, with obfuscation of PII in transit logs and token-level cost breakdowns for billing.
- Retention: model inputs must be ephemeral by default; however some legal/regulatory transcripts may need 7 years retention in an archival store.
- Failover: cross-region warm-standby acceptable if encrypted at rest and in transit; require manual failover trigger for jurisdictional constraints.

What we attached / included
- redwood-residency-summary.pdf — quick matrix of region pin options, failover modes (automatic vs manual), and their operational tradeoffs.
- sunrise-mapping-template.xlsx — simple template to map which data classes need US-only handling, which can be replicated to EU for analytics, and which are allowed in APAC.

Open questions we committed to answering
1) Can we guarantee that inference for pinned customers never leaves the selected region (US) even for autoscaling or shard placement? Short answer: yes for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted customers get strong region affinity with warm-standby patterns — we detail tradeoffs below.
2) Does Redwood persist request/response in logs or KV caches by default? We do not persist user content in long-term logs by default; audit logs capture metadata and hashed IDs. We offer configurable policies to redact or omit request/response content and to enforce zero retention.
3) What is the RPO/RTO for a cross-region warm standby and what encryption/KMS guarantees are available? See attachment; typical warm-standby RPO is ~15m with RTO depending on pre-warmed capacity. KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) supported for Private and Dedicated.

Next steps
- Can you confirm which of the three data classes in the attached template must be US-only (column B)? Please fill and return the template by EOD Wednesday so we can prepare an internal runbook.
- I'll schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive with Ben (solutions) and Marissa (account lead) for Thursday; please tell us preferred windows.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com] | +1 650-555-0142

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@sunrisehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@sunrisehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency constraints & logs — Sunrise Health follow-up

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security team (I've collated answers we need before the deep dive):

1) "Never leaves region": under what exact conditions would hosted inference route to EU/APAC? We need a written list of fallback triggers (e.g., total capacity breach, incident recovery) and an assurance that fallback can be disabled.
2) Audit logs: if we ask for request/response exclusion in logs, can we still get token-level cost reports and latency percentiles for billing and SLA?
3) Data retention exceptions: we have a small set of court-ordered transcripts (legal holds). Can Redwood place those specific items in a seven-year WORM archive while retaining zero retention for everything else?

We're working on filling the mapping template today. For the technical session Thursday, 10:00–11:00 AM PT works for us.

— Alex
Director of Platform Security | Sunrise Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@sunrisehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: residency constraints & logs — Sunrise Health follow-up

Alex — answers inline below, and I've attached a short one-pager that maps options to operational impact. Ben and I will cover these in the technical deep-dive.

1) Fallback triggers and guarantees- Hosted: default is region affinity with warm-standby — we document three explicit fallback triggers: (a) regional capacity exhaustion beyond configured burst threshold, (b) region-wide provider outage with automated fallback allowed, (c) customer-requested manual failover for operational reasons. Hosted customers can opt-out of automatic fallback; opting out may increase latency and reduce failover automation.
- Dedicated/Private: pinning is enforced at the orchestration layer — workloads will not be scheduled outside the pinned region unless the customer authorizes it.

2) Audit logs vs billing telemetry- Yes — we can separate telemetry streams. Billing and performance metrics (token counts, latency percentiles, error rates) are retained independently and can be provided without storing raw request/response bodies. We also support hashed identifiers to map billing to requests without exposing content.

3) Legal-hold / WORM archival- We support selective retention policies: items flagged for legal-hold can be archived to an immutable (WORM) store for the required retention period while default retention remains zero. This is available on Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we provide a managed archive option with contractual controls.

Attachments: redwood-residency-summary.pdf (summary, 2 pages) — uploaded to shared Drive link; sunrise-mapping-template.xlsx — template to return filled.

Confirmed: Thursday 10:00–10:30 AM PT for the technical call (we'll request 30 minutes).

Thanks — Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Sunrise Health — prep items before Thu technical call

Team — quick internal checklist before the 10:00 AM PT deep-dive: 

- Ben: be prepared to demo configuration UI for region pinning + show the orchestration enforcement (Dedicated private demo + hosted affinity toggle). Bring an example of KMS CMK workflow.
- Jordan: prioritize the mapping template rows we want Sunrise to fill during the call; identify any items that would trigger an enterprise legal review.
- Marissa: I'll draft a short SOW snippet covering WORM archival and opt-out of automatic fallback to share after the call.

If we need pre-approved language for hosted customers around capacity-triggered fallback, I'll pull the standard clause from legal and attach to the HubSpot deal.

Marissa
Director, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
